item.title: No winter shopping? Bayern Bosses reveal their stance after injury setbacks
item.description: No winter shopping? Bayern Bosses reveal their stance after injury setbacks Bayern Munich are not planning to enter the January transfer market despite their recent injury problems, according to club president Herbert Hainer. Speaking at Saturday's Annual General Meeting, Hainer admitted that the current situation was not anticipated but insisted that the club does not believe immediate reinforcements are necessary. Luis Díaz is expected to return soon, while Alphonso Davies could be back to full fitness within two weeks. Serge Gnabry is also gradually returning to training. "Therefore, I don't think we need to react in the winter transfer window," Hainer explained. However, the Bayern president acknowledged that circumstances can change quickly, particularly after the club suffered two further injury setbacks, Harry Kane and Michael OIise are both unavailable for the time being, ahead of the AGM. Hainer made it clear that Bayern would be financially capable of reacting if necessary, but stressed that this was not their preferred approach. The club's leadership also remains cautious about January business, with Hainer pointing out that Bayern have not enjoyed much success with signings made during the winter window or in the final days of transfer periods. For now, the Bundesliga leaders are hoping their injured players can return soon enough to avoid the need for additional reinforcements.

item.title: Williams to stay in charge of Swans for Boro trip
item.description: Ashley Williams played more than 350 games for Swansea across eight years [Huw Evans Picture Agency] Ashley Williams will remain at the helm for Swansea City's trip to Middlesbrough on Tuesday after taking a point against West Bromwich Albion in his first game as interim boss. Swansea started life after Vitor Matos by coming from behind twice in a chaotic 2-2 draw with the Baggies at the Swansea.com Stadium. Williams, who was seen having a lengthy discussion with Swansea chief executive Tom Gorringe after the game, says he has been told he will remain in charge for the midweek trip to face Championship leaders Boro. "I will go to Middlesbrough with the team," Swansea's interim boss said. "I will be concentrating on the build-up to Middlesbrough and the Middlesbrough game, and that is it at that point. "I don't know what happens [after that]. I'm not too interested, if I'm being deadly honest, because all eyes are on Middlesbrough after this. I can tell you that much, and that's it at this point." Williams is leading a caretaker management team also featuring fellow Swansea old boys Leon Britton, Joe Allen and Kristian O'Leary following this week's shock departure of Vitor Matos. The 42-year-old, who has primarily worked as a pundit since retiring as a player, said he "absolutely loved" the experience of leading Swansea from the touchline. "To be back here as well was special, and to be with this set of players at this football club is special," he added. Eli Just scored his first goal for Swanse [Huw Evans Picture Agency] "When you're in it, you're concentrating so much that that's all you're thinking about. But when the dust settles and I digest it, maybe this evening or whenever, it's a really proud moment for me. "Even when we went a goal down, I was enjoying it. I was in it with the players. "I wanted them to be aware of me. I wanted them to see me and hear me. If we're suffering for a minute, I'm with them. If we score, I'm with them and I'm happy. It was really nice to feel connected with the team and the whole stadium." Williams' side endured the worst possible start as Isaac Price gave West Brom a seventh-minute lead, but they quickly replied through Moussa Yeo. Rabby Nzingoula then restored Albion's lead before Baggies forward Isaac Price's Panenka penalty was saved by Lawrence Vigouroux. Eli Just swiftly made it 2-2, with the New Zealander also hitting the bar after Melker Widell had struck the post, though Swansea ended up feeling relieved to claim a point as West Brom pushed hard for a second-half winner. "It was end-to-end and very frantic," Williams said. "But my natural thought is just how proud I am of the players and the fans. "To respond after a week like this, an uncertain week, was impressive. Maybe we saw that uncertainty in our team at the start, in the first few minutes, but they recovered themselves." item.title: 'Fragile' Chelsea need to be tougher, says Alonso
item.description: Chelsea suffered an embarrassing home defeat against Leeds (Henry NICHOLLS) Xabi Alonso warned his "fragile" Chelsea flops to toughen up after their humiliating 4-1 home defeat against Leeds on Saturday. Alonso's side were ripped apart by rampant Leeds, who savoured their first Premier League win at Stamford Bridge in 27 years. Chelsea scored six in a League Cup win against Leeds in September, but Daniel Farke's men erased that painful result with a superb display on their return to west London. The Blues are languishing in eighth place after a fifth defeat in their 11 league games under Alonso. Only three teams in the Premier League have conceded more goals than the 20 allowed by Chelsea, prompting Alonso to question his players' mentality. "We need to be tougher. It's something mandatory in this competition," the former Liverpool midfielder said. "Today we were in a fragile moment mentally. Confidence that, when we receive a punch, we will not recover." Making his full debut in Alonso's latest bid to find a stand-in for injured striker Joao Pedro, Emmanuel Emegha fired Chelsea ahead in the 25th minute. Yet within three minutes they gifted an equaliser to Noah Okafor, who punished static defending to lash home. Morgan Rogers conceded a penalty eight minutes into the second half and Dominic Calvert-Lewin converted to put Leeds in front. Swiss striker Okafor quickly made it three in the 58th minute and Brenden Aaronson got a fourth in stoppage-time to leave Chelsea in turmoil. Chelsea were booed off at half-time and again at the final whistle as furious fans showed their displeasure. Alonso pointed to the loss of midfielder Moises Caicedo, forced off injured midway through the first half, as the turning point in the game. "After we lost Moises we lost completely the momentum. Until then we were doing OK, but from that moment they started believing and we started not believing," he said. "After that, we never got the good feeling and were not able to come from the pressure. It completely changed." Over a miserable five-match spell, the Blues have lost to Tottenham, Sunderland and Leeds, while also crashing out of the League Cup against Liverpool. While it is too soon to suggest Alonso is in danger of the sack, the Spaniard has endured a disappointing start to his first spell as a Premier League manager. Failing to beat struggling pair Nottingham Forest and Crystal Palace in their next two games would undoubtedly turn the heat up on the former Real Madrid and Bayer Leverkusen boss. "I'm not feeling let down. We do it as a team, as a collective. We need to support each other. We need to find solutions to do better because this will happen," Alonso said. "There were moments that we were not competing at the level required. But the physicality, the duels, it's not the only explanation. The mentality part we can do better." smg/nf

item.title: Nations Championship schedule, results and finals weekend permutations
item.description: Rugby’s Nations Championship has reached its last weekend of pool play with the finals weekend fate of the world’s top teams becoming clear. The new competition pits the Six Nations sides against the four Rugby Championship competitors, plus Japan and Fiji, across six matches split evenly across the July and November Test windows. The results of those games will determine each of the 12 teams’ seedings for the finals weekend at Twickenham’s Allianz Stadium , with six matches contested over two days and both team and hemisphere silverware up for grabs. Each entrant will be matched against the equivalent qualifier from the other pool to decide overall placings at the conclusion of a busy year of international action – and South Africa have pipped New Zealand to top spot in their pool with a bonus point in defeat to Ireland. Here’s the full competition schedule, and how the tables stand ahead of finals weekend. What is the Nations Championship? Announced during the 2023 Rugby World Cup, the new competition will be held every other year and replaces the traditional summer tours and Autumn Nations Series. It is designed to add context to the international calendar, with Fiji and Japan invited to join the Six Nations and Rugby Championship sides to form a top 12. Promotion and relegation is planned for the future with the second-tier Nations Cup, though will not take place in 2026. The entrants are: Northern Hemisphere : France, Ireland, Scotland, Italy, England, Wales. Southern Hemisphere: South Africa, New Zealand, Argentina, Australia, Fiji, Japan. What about the finals weekend? The first finals weekend will be held at Twickenham on the last weekend (27 to 29) of November. Three days of double-headers will be held at the ground, with the first-placed finisher of the Six Nations sides meeting whoever tops the other pool, and so on and so forth down the rankings. The winner of that marquee match will lift the first Nations Championship trophy, while whichever hemisphere – a term used loosely with Japan included in the “southern” section and Fiji hosting their games in the United Kingdom – wins more final matches will also be crowned. item.title: Why Jose Mourinho has benched Vinicius Jr. at Real Madrid as Yan Diomande stars on the left
item.description: Why Jose Mourinho has benched Vinicius Jr. at Real Madrid as Yan Diomande stars on the left originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The time has come to take a hard look at Vinicius Jr's starting position at Real Madrid . There is no debating that Vini is one of the best left wingers in the world. That has not changed in the first few months of the 2026/27 season. However, after Vini served his four-game La Liga suspension for pulling the hair of Nathan Saliba, there is now also no debating that Real Madrid are better without the Brazilian on the field. That is just a fact. Fans have, over the last three weeks, enjoyed the rare opportunity of seeing Real Madrid play with and without Vini in alternating matches, as he was ineligible to compete in league play but eligible to play in Champions League matches. What resulted was a clear juxtaposition — Real Madrid were better in almost every single aspect without Vini. In the La Liga matches, Jose Mourinho started Yan Diomande at his more natural left wing position, with Arda Guler as an inside forward on the right. This allowed Diomande to dazzle on the ball out wide left, while Guler cut inside as a quasi-midfielder, allowing Federico Valverde or Denzel Dumfries to overlap down the right. The balance in this setup is exceptional. Diomande's willingness and capability to track back and defend makes the whole thing work, as he stays out of Kylian Mbappe's way up front and helps out Marc Cucurella, giving Real Madrid more dynamism. While Diomande gets lots of credit for Madrid's excellent performances without Vini, and deservingly so, Guler has also flown spectacularly under the radar in this setup. The Turkey international has been nothing short of sensational this season, flourishing in this inside forward role. His relationship with Mbappe has been especially strong, proven as Mbappe responded to Guler's recent contract renewal by saying on social media, "I will sleep better tonight." According to Opta, Guler leads La Liga in chances created so far this season with 42, averaging 5.08 per 90 minutes. To put that into perspective: Kevin De Bruyne's best Premier League season in 2019/20, where he racked up an outrageous 20 assists, saw him create 4.32 chances per 90 minutes. item.title: NASCAR Star Tries Bull Riding, Immediately Regrets It
item.description: Kansas City Outlaws bull rider Cassio Dias rides Ricky Vaughn during the championship round on Sunday, April 7, 2024, at Denny Sanford Premier Center in Sioux Falls. NASCAR driver Noah Gragson thought trying bull riding would be an exciting change of pace. Instead, his trip to Davis Rodeo Ranch in North Carolina left him sore for an entire week. The Front Row Motorsports driver climbed aboard two bulls and quickly discovered that handling a race car and staying on a bucking bull require very different skills. Speaking on This Cowboy Life podcast , Gragson described how the soreness began shortly after the experience. “I was pretty good there for a couple hours, and then I got to Olive Garden. We went to Olive Garden afterward in Salisbury, and my neck started getting kind of sore,” he said. A Week of Sore Muscles Gragson said the discomfort worsened the following day. He struggled to raise his arm and described his shoulder as “killing me for the last week.” The soreness also spread through his abdomen and groin, involving what he called “muscles I’ve never used before.” His introduction to bull riding involved two attempts. The first bull offered little resistance, but the second was considerably tougher. Gragson lasted approximately two seconds before getting thrown off. He also described being dashboarded during the experience. By the time he spoke on the podcast, about a week later, he said he was finally somewhat back to normal. Nov 8, 2026; Homestead, Florida, USA; NASCAR Cup Series driver Noah Gragson (4) during the NASCAR Cup Series Championship Race at Homestead-Miami Speedway. Mandatory Credit: Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images Unconventional Recovery Methods Gragson even found an unusual way to get some relief during a visit to the Cosmopolitan Casino. He described receiving a massage while leaning over a blackjack table, paying $2 per minute for treatment focused on his neck and back. He credited the massage with helping his traps and neck finally feel better. Gragson finally recovered enough to move freely again after a week of pain. His experience on the ranch in North Carolina remains a painful memory for the NASCAR star : “That was the craziest experience I’ve ever had.”

item.title: Half a million! Bayern reach historic membership milestone among other records
item.description: Half a million! Bayern reach historic membership milestone among other records FC Bayern Munich have announced that they now have 500,000 registered members , making them the world's largest sports club by registered membership. Their members come from 152 different countries. The announcement was one of several highlights at Saturday's Annual General Meeting, where the club also revealed record financial results for the 2025/26 financial year. Bayern generated a turnover of €988.2 million , an increase of approximately €10 million compared to the previous year. Operating profit rose to €190.8 million, while the club recorded a consolidated net profit of €22.8 million. CEO Jan-Christian Dreesen described the figures as another record year, emphasising the importance of financial discipline and sustainable investment. He also addressed ticket prices, insisting that football must remain affordable for supporters despite the growing commercial demands of the sport. A regular Bundesliga ticket at Bayern currently costs around €80, a price the club has maintained for several years. Meanwhile, president Herbert Hainer praised the club's growing international appeal and highlighted the importance of its partnership with German family-owned business Viessmann. There was also a special message from head coach Vincent Kompany, who thanked the supporters for their backing and described how his family had quickly come to feel at home in Munich.

item.title: Michigan Makes Official Andrew Marsh Decision Following Troubling Week
item.description: The Michigan Wolverines have made their decision on wide receiver Andrew Marsh , and it’s not the news fans were hoping for ahead of Saturday’s showdown against No. 4 UCLA. After being listed as questionable throughout the week, Marsh has officially been ruled OUT for Michigan’s final home game of the 2026 season. According to the Big Ten’s final game-day availability report, Marsh is one of 10 Wolverines who will not suit up against the undefeated Bruins. The news comes at an especially difficult time for Michigan, which is already dealing with significant injuries and desperately needs a victory to become bowl eligible. Oregon defensive back Brandon Finney Jr., right, breaks up a pass intended for Michigan wide receiver Andrew Marsh as the Oregon Ducks host the Michigan Wolverines on Nov. 14, 2026, at Autzen Stadium in Eugene, Oregon. Credit: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Andrew Marsh Ruled Out Amid Off-Field Situation Marsh’s availability had been uncertain throughout the week, but not solely because of injury concerns. On Thursday, news surfaced that the sophomore receiver was facing a misdemeanor indecent exposure charge stemming from an alleged incident earlier this year. Michigan subsequently released a statement acknowledging the situation , although the university did not publicly confirm whether the legal matter would affect his playing status. The charge remains an allegation, and the final availability report does not specify why Marsh has been ruled out. According to Reuters , Michigan officials said they had recently become aware of the incident. The program has not publicly announced a suspension in connection with the matter. Michigan’s Offense Takes Another Major Hit Losing Marsh is a significant blow for a Michigan offense that has struggled to consistently move the football this season. Through 10 games, Marsh has recorded 47 receptions for 444 yards and one touchdown, making him one of the Wolverines’ most important receiving options. Unfortunately, he isn’t the only receiver unavailable against UCLA. JJ Buchanan, Jaylen Pile, and Braydon Alford are also listed as out on Saturday’s final availability report, leaving Michigan extremely thin at the position. The Wolverines are also missing offensive linemen Ace Hamilton, Andrew Sprague, and Blake Frazier, along with running back Micah Ka’apana and defensive ends Julius Holly and Nate Marshall. Michigan’s previous injury report already revealed serious concerns , and Saturday’s update only makes the situation more difficult. Defensive tackle Enow Etta and running back Jordan Marshall are listed as game-time decisions, meaning Michigan could be dealing with additional absences. Head coach Kyle Whittingham now faces an enormous challenge as the 5-5 Wolverines prepare to host undefeated UCLA. item.title: De Zerbi not surprised by 'special' Williams-Barnett
item.description: Luca Williams-Barnett scored on his first Premier League start (Ben Stansall) Tottenham boss Roberto De Zerbi hailed 18-year-old Luca Williams-Barnett as a "special player" after he scored and assisted on his first Premier League start in a 2-0 win over Ipswich on Saturday. The teenager stole the show as Tottenham's upturn continued with a fourth win in five games to climb to ninth in the Premier League table and within three points of the top four. "Luca Barnett is a special player. I am not surprised because his talent is bigger than you think," said De Zerbi in his post-match press conference. The Italian said he had taken the decision to give Williams-Barnett a full debut 10 days ago after he showed flashes of promise in two cameo substitute appearances against Crystal Palace and Leeds. "Yesterday evening when I gave the first eleven... I said to the other players remember the first game, the debut of you (Williams-Barnett) and help the kid tomorrow because he is one of us and if he plays well, we have more chances to win the game." Williams-Barnett showed a poacher's instinct to meet Pedro Porro's cross at the back post to open the scoring on 15 minutes. The winger then ran from inside his own half before producing a perfect cross for Dominic Solanke to tap in Tottenham's second. De Zerbi did not hold back on comparing the England under-19 international to some of the biggest stars in world football if he can match their workrate. "The first day I spoke with Luca and I asked him two things," added De Zerbi. "To play like he plays on the park with his friends with the same freedom and to play and to work hard without the ball like (Ousmane) Dembele, like Raphinha, like (Lamine) Yamal because football is going in a different way and the first defenders are really the attackers. item.title: Big blow for Bangladesh! Star player ruled out of second Test against South Africa
item.description: Bangladesh have suffered a major setback ahead of the second Test against South Africa, with experienced batter Mushfiqur Rahim ruled out of the series finale due to a groin injury. The second Test is scheduled to begin at Centurion on November 23, with Bangladesh needing a victory to level the two-match series after going 1-0 down in Johannesburg. Mushfiqur sustained the injury during the opening Test at the Wanderers, where he complained of acute pain in his left groin. A subsequent MRI scan confirmed inflammation and irritation around the bony pelvis, forcing the team management to rule him out of the upcoming contest. Bangladesh national team physiotherapist Bayjedul Islam Khan confirmed the development, explaining that the veteran batter needs immediate rest and a rehabilitation programme to prevent the injury from worsening. "Mushfiqur complained of acute pain in the left groin region during the first Test match. Following the Test, he underwent an MRI scan and the results confirmed some inflammation and irritation around the bony pelvis," Khan said. "He requires immediate rest and targeted rehabilitation to manage the stress response and prevent further aggravation and is unavailable for the second Test," he added. Mushfiqur's absence comes at a difficult time for Bangladesh, who will be keen to bounce back after suffering a nine-wicket defeat in the series opener. The veteran batter had scored 22 in the first innings and 22 in the second innings of the Johannesburg Test. Meanwhile, South Africa have also been dealt an injury setback, with captain Temba Bavuma ruled out of the second Test due to a calf strain. Bavuma is expected to remain with the squad, while Aiden Markram is likely to take over the captaincy. Tony de Zorzi is tipped to come into the playing XI as his replacement. Bangladesh face uphill task to level series The opening Test at the Wanderers saw Bangladesh produce a spirited fightback after an early batting collapse. From 22/3 and later 121/5, they recovered through centuries from Towhid Hridoy (137) and Litton Das (120), who put together a record 206-run partnership for the sixth wicket to take the visitors to 400. South Africa responded with a formidable 557, powered by maiden Test centuries from Marques Ackerman (157) and Ryan Rickelton (102), while Zubayr Hamza contributed 83 and Kagiso Rabada struck a career-best 72. Bangladesh fought back with the ball, but South Africa secured a sizeable 157-run first-innings advantage. In their second innings, the visitors struggled against Rabada and Simon Harmer, eventually being bowled out for 168. Harmer was the chief destroyer with figures of 6/51, while Rabada claimed three wickets. South Africa were left with a modest target of 12 runs and completed the chase to register a nine-wicket victory, taking a 1-0 lead in the series.

item.title: UFC Qatar results: Ikram Aliskerov puts on suffocating grappling performance to beat Jared Cannonier
item.description: Ikram Aliskerov wins his fourth in a row (Photo by Ed Mulholland/Zuffa LLC) Ikram Aliskerov couldn’t quite get the submission but he used his grappling to drown Jared Cannonier over three rounds to kick off the UFC Qatar main card on Saturday. While he did show off some solid striking early, Aliskerov eventually turned to his wrestling with repeated takedowns and multiple submission attempts to put Cannonier away. The judges scored the fight 30-27 across the board as Aliskerov got the job done by unanimouos decision. Cannonier was aggressive to start, throwing out a good lead jab and mixing in some kicks to the legs. Aliskerov got his attention midway through the round with a hard shot that had Cannonier rattled briefly. Aliskerov’s combinations were starting to connect and his confidence surged as he sought to do damage on the former title challenger. He also scored a takedown to mix things up as the fight moved into the second round. A fence grab from Aliskerov forced a standup from the referee as the action continued back on the feet. But Aliskerov was quick to return to the takedown as he started looking for an arm triangle choke on the ground, although Cannonier defended effectively. Aliskerov eventually hopped on the back and nearly locked on a rear-naked choke but time ran out on the Russian. With five minutes remaining, Aliskerov took Cannonier down again as he sought to control the action while looking to advance his position. Aliskerov snatched onto a kimura but Cannonier resisted and broke free but he was still stuck on the ground. That ground attack allowed Aliskerov to cruise to victory as he gets his fourth win in a row overall while Cannonier suffers a third straight defeat.

item.title: PSG lose Doue to knee injury in Ligue 1 win at Nice
item.description: Desire Doue lies on the ground in agony after going down with a knee injury in PSG's Ligue 1 win at Nice on Saturday (Valery HACHE) Paris Saint-Germain star Desire Doue was stretchered off in tears after suffering what looked like a nasty knee injury as the reigning French and European champions beat Nice 3-2 in Ligue 1 on Saturday. Doue went down after twisting awkwardly late in the first half as he tried to control the ball, shortly after scoring to put PSG 2-1 ahead. He looked in agony as he clutched his right knee, and the match was stopped for five minutes to allow Doue to receive treatment before being carried off to a backdrop of applause from the crowd at the Allianz Riviera stadium. PSG will now be dreading discovering the extent of the injury, having lost Khvicha Kvaratskhelia to a ruptured anterior cruciate ligament in his right knee playing against Barcelona last month. The Georgian winger is unlikely to return this season, and Doue looks set for a significant spell on the sidelines too. The 21-year-old French international, who can play on the wing or in midfield, has been arguably PSG's best player this season after playing a key role in PSG's Champions League triumphs in each of the last two campaigns. He has notably scored three goals in three Champions League appearances this season for PSG, who sold Bradley Barcola to Liverpool at the beginning of the campaign and have seen Ousmane Dembele struggle with his fitness recently. Earlier, Algerian international Mohamed Amoura had given Nice the lead only for Senny Mayulu to equalise with a penalty awarded after a VAR check following a handball in the home box. Doue -- who was wearing a mouthguard after one of his teeth became dislodged while playing for France against Italy during the international break -- put PSG ahead a minute after that goal, turning in at the back post from an Achraf Hakimi assist for his sixth of the season in all competitions. His replacement Ferran Torres scored PSG's third in the 85th minute, controlling in the box before finishing on the turn for his eighth goal of the season -- but first in two months. Ali Abdi pulled one back for Nice in stoppage time, but their run of three straight wins was ended as PSG made it 12 victories on the bounce. Eight of those wins have come in Ligue 1, in which PSG are now five points clear at the top from Lille, who host Lyon later. Nice are sixth. as/nf

item.title: Weigman out, Keisean Henderson to make first career start vs. West Virginia
item.description: Keisean Henderson officially gets the start vs. West Virginia (Photo by Tim Warner/Getty Images) (Tim Warner/Getty Images) A major change is coming for the University of Houston football program as it prepares to take on West Virginia on Saturday. Keisean Henderson , the first five-star QB recruit in school history, is set to start after incumbent starter Conner Weigman was ruled out with an undisclosed injury he suffered against Colorado. ESPN College Football insider Pete Thamel confirmed the news in a post on X early Saturday morning. The loss to Colorado was a Friday night nightmare for the Cougars and officially dashed their College Football Playoff and Big 12 Championship hopes. Weigman appeared on the injury report Friday and warmed up ahead of Saturday's kickoff but couldn't play. All season, Weigman has been the engine for the Cougars offense, throwing for 2,552 yards and 25 touchdowns, while also rushing for seven rushing touchdowns. Henderson, who ended his high school career at Spring as one of the nation's top recruits, has gotten time on the field this season. In limited duty behind center, he's thrown eight passes, completed six of them for two touchdowns and had an electrifying 54-yard TD run vs. Southern University. Cougars coach Willie Fritz has been high on Henderson since camp, touting that he had two of the best quarterbacks in the country with Henderson and Weigman. For now, as the Cougars look to push to finish the regular season with nine wins, he turns to the freshman everyone wants to see. "Everybody is asking if we are going to have a package for Keisean," Fritz said during Big 12 media days in July. "We are throwing the whole package at him; he's got to learn how to do everything. It is very rare that you go through a season with only one quarterback." He added, "We are really blessed that we have two outstanding quarterbacks with Conner Weigman and Keisean Henderson." How ironic that in late November, Fritz' prophecy about using bout quarterbacks for stats has come true. item.title: How Columbus Crew turned it all around to set up MLS playoff showdown vs. Messi
item.description: It wasn’t working. Issa Tall had to admit that. Well, he didn’t really have to. The results told the story for him. The Columbus Crew didn’t win in its first five MLS matches. By the World Cup break, 15 games in, they’d only added two more. There needed to be changes, and they needed to be big. The Crew general manager moved quickly. In May, he fired coach Henrik Rydström, his first coaching hire as the Crew’s chief soccer officer, though he was quick to point out he was involved with previous hires including bringing in Wilfried Nancy. He spent big in the summer, revamping the Crew’s attack and adding pieces while bidding farewell to some regulars. Ten players arrived, and eight went out. It worked. The Crew turned the boat around, going from worst in the Eastern Conference to closing the season on a six-game win streak and having won eight of their last nine. That was enough not only to jump out of Thursday’s wild card match but to set up a First Round playoff series with Inter Miami, the reigning champion led by Lionel Messi. They also pushed to the U.S. Open Cup final, falling to St. Louis City in a penalty shootout. All of it led Tall to believe he made the right decisions, moving on quickly from the coach he thought was the right man for the job. “Some people could’ve waited the full year. Maybe it would’ve been safer, but that’s not me. That’s not us as a club. That’s not even the way we play!” Tall told USA TODAY Sports ahead of the playoffs. “You see how we are bold and are not afraid of taking risk. At the end of the day, it wasn’t even a risk necessarily. It was necessary for our players, for our club as a whole and I think ultimately we made the right decision to do it at that time.” Tall still stands by Rydström as a good coach, something he’s proving while leading Hammarby in Sweden which currently sits atop of the table after running off five consecutive wins. But he wasn’t the right fit for the Crew in the post-Nancy era. The Crew turned to Courtois, a former Crew academy and MLS Next Pro coach who continued the idea first expressed on the field so successfully by Nancy’s teams. item.title: Gotham FC’s title defense comes to crushing end in semifinal loss after venue change
item.description: They came by car, by the special-event X80 bus, by bike if they were feeling sporty. They came in layers, in beanies and scarves, with Gotham’s black-and-sky-blue colors on top. They came on behalf of those who couldn’t come, capacity being reduced at this impromptu change of venue, each one trying to make noise for five. And then, 25 miles and 20,000 seats removed from their regular destination at New Jersey’s Sports Illustrated Stadium, huddled in the bleachers by a blue track ringing an immaculate pitch at Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island, in the shadow of the old Psychiatric Center and with the light fading over the Costco across the river, 5,000 devoted souls Sunday afternoon watched Gotham’s NWSL title defense end in a 2-1 semifinal loss to the Kansas City Current. “We lost today because we weren’t the better team,” Gotham winger and oracle Midge Purce said. “That being said, I would say it’s inexcusable. It’s not what you want in a professional league. It’s not what you want for women who are progressing in the United States and supposed to be one of the best leagues in the entire world. I think it’s a bad look for everyone involved. And we always want to be at Sports Illustrated in front of our fans when we earned that right throughout the season. item.title: Beckham to be inducted into US Soccer Hall of Fame
item.description: David Beckham was knighted by King Charles in 2025 [Getty Images] David Beckham will be inducted into the United States' National Soccer Hall of Fame as part of its 2027 class. The former Manchester United and England midfielder, 51, made headlines in 2007 when he moved to Los Angeles from Spanish giants Real Madrid to join Major League Soccer (MLS) side LA Galaxy on a five-year contract. He made 124 appearances in all competitions for Galaxy, scoring 20 goals, and twice won both the MLS Cup and Supporters' Shield. Beckham's six seasons at Galaxy helped to raise the global profile of MLS and following his retirement in 2013, he became co-owner of MLS club Inter Miami, who signed Argentina World Cup winner Lionel Messi in 2023. His induction ceremony is set to take place on 16 April 2027 in Frisco, Texas. David Beckham's deal with LA Galaxy in 2007 was reportedly worth £128m [Getty Images] He was told the news he had been chosen on the veterans' ballot at an MLS board of governors' meeting on Thursday and said his time in the US has been "an incredible journey". Beckham, who had two loan spells with AC Milan in 2009 and 2010 while at Galaxy, added: "I'm looking to build this league and this sport in this great country for a long time." Meanwhile, former US internationals Megan Rapinoe and Julie Ertz have also been voted into the Hall of Fame in their first year of eligibility. Ballon d'Or winner Rapinoe, 41, and midfielder Ertz, 34, lifted the Women’s World Cup twice with with the US in 2015 and 2019. "To be alongside all the greatest players that have played for us, and played for our country alongside a bunch of my team-mates and friends, recognised like that in this way just means you were successful and a part of great teams," Rapinoe wrote on Instagram. item.title: Messi makes history with MLS Golden Boot
item.description: Messi retired from international football with Argentina earlier this year [Getty Images] Inter Miami forward Lionel Messi has become the first player in MLS history to win the Golden Boot in consecutive seasons. The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner scored 26 goals in 31 appearances, four clear of FC Dallas striker Peter Musa and five more than Nashville's English forward Sam Surridge. Messi becomes only the sixth player to land the award twice, joining a list that includes former Charlton Athletic and Southampton striker Bradley Wright-Phillips. In addition to his goals, the 39-year-old notched 17 assists over the course of the MLS season, ensuring his 43 goal contributions was also a league best for the second year in a row. And the World Cup winner could soon make more history as he bids to become the first three-time Landon Donovan MLS MVP winner. The former Argentina forward landed the award in 2024 as Inter Miami won the Supporters' Shield title and also in 2025 as they won the MLS Cup. Despite Messi's magic, Miami weren't able to land top spot in the MLS Eastern Conference, with the team finishing 17 points behind Surridge's Nashville. They will now face Columbus Crew over three games in the first round of the MLS Cup play-offs which begin later this month. item.title: On MLS Decision Day, D.C. United faces a familiar reality: Another season of failure
item.description: WASHINGTON — All around Major League Soccer , from Montreal to Miami and Seattle to San Diego, Saturday was Decision Day — the last act in an 8½-month production. While three playoff berths were in the balance, teams with guaranteed spots sought to improve their place. It's a day marked by desperation, scoreboard-watching and playoff-planning. At Audi Field, however, Decision Day felt more like Derision Day. For the seventh consecutive year, D.C. United, once a showpiece of a blossoming league, has no playoff plans — a near impossibility in a league that distributes postseason passes like a guy on a New York street corner handing out flyers for discount mattresses. Only Toronto FC's eight-year rut, starting with its 2007 expansion campaign, lasted longer. United wasn't even in the mix on Decision Day, its fate having been decided 10 days earlier. The lowly finale was against another failed side, New York City FC, which claimed a 1-0 victory on a late goal. While 2026 was an anomaly for the New Yorkers, it was the norm in the nation's capital. D.C. added another sad chapter to a rotten story under an ownership group, led by Jason Levien and Steve Kaplan, that has dragged the organization into irrelevance in not just the prospering league but in the local market and the ascending sport. The public-address announcer introduces the team as "your four-time MLS Cup champions," but he's been saying that for a long time. Given the league's evolution, it feels even longer. United's last title, in 2004, came in a 10-team operation — one-third the current landscape. Since then, 13 different clubs have hoisted the trophy. Less than two miles north of Audi Field, the U.S. Capitol witnessed a historic sea change Tuesday with a political wave that swept the ruling party out of office. Local soccer fans have had no such luck with those in power at Audi Field. Under the current regime … United hasn't won a playoff game in 11 years and hasn't advanced to the conference finals in 14. Twelve years have passed since it won at least half its 34 matches. United's only trophy in recent memory was the 2013 U.S. Open Cup, which came amid a horrific, three-win regular season. D.C. is on its fourth head coach since Ben Olsen's departure in late 2020 and its second head of soccer operations in four years. The current director, Erkut Sogut — an agent best known for representing former German star Mesut Özil — was hired last fall without any experience working for a team. Another goal conceded, another season to forget. Keisuke Kurokawa's frustration summed up D.C. United's latest disappointing chapter.
